why.text: Steep slopes of greywacke and slate in a narrow river valley give mostly red wines with fine aromas and high minerality.

styles.text: Mostly red wines, with traditional rosé and white; base wines can also become Sekt b.A. and Qualitätsperlwein.

climate.text: Mean daily temperature 9.8 °C, about 650 mm rain a year and about 1,450 hours of sunshine. Long growing season.

soil.text: Mostly greywacke sandstone with some clay slate, hard in the west and deeply weathered in the east. Gravel, loam and loess on river terraces.

altitude.text: Valley floor about 150 m in the west and about 100 m in the east, with slopes 150 to 200 m high. 69% of vineyards slope over 30%.

tastes.text: Reds: light to dark ruby, blueberry, dried fruit, strawberry and cherry, dense. Rosés: fresh, lighter, less tannin. Whites: peach and citrus, clearly noticeable acidity.

styles.name: Kabinett
styles.text: Prädikat wine, at least 10.0% potential alcohol for whites, 10.6% for reds.

styles.name: Trockenbeerenauslese
styles.text: Prädikat wine needing at least 21.5% potential alcohol (150° Öchsle).

styles.name: Eiswein
styles.text: Prädikat wine of at least 15.3% potential alcohol (110° Öchsle); no enrichment allowed.

styles.name: Sekt b.A.
styles.text: Sparkling wine; bottle-fermented ones mature at least nine months on the bottle.
